headline: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
body: U.S. President Donald Trump has intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, following his recent ouster
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

U.S. President Donald Trump saw little choice but to fight to reinstate Jensen Huang at AI behemoth Nvidia .

The president has staked the nation's economic growth on artificial intelligence, and worried Mr. Huang's ouster was not only tanking the stock market — but also risked putting the U.S. behind Beijing in the race for dominance in the field if Mr. Huang, widely seen by backers and critics as a generational talent in artificial intelligence, were to be poached by a Chinese firm.

And the president, a thrice-married man and real estate maven who has seen his own marital infidelity scrutinised in the press, bristled at Mr. Huang being ousted from the company he built because of extramarital affairs, including one with an executive at a Singapore-based company who U.S. officials suspect was a Chinese spy.

So Mr. Trump engaged in an extraordinary level of behind-the-scenes maneuvering to reinstate Mr. Huang, starting almost immediately after the CEO's fall from grace when he resigned on November 12 as reports trickled out about a trio of affairs.

The U.S. president stated plainly in a CNBC interview on Monday he used his considerable sway to get Mr. Huang his job back. “I spoke to them,” Trump said of the company's board of directors. “Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them.”

Monday's reinstatement was a remarkable turnaround by Nvidia's board, which had insisted days after Mr. Huang’s ouster that it was not considering such a move, even as Trump pushed for it and thousands signed an online petition calling for Huang’s return.

Sales of Grand Theft Auto VI generated a record with $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales, maker Rockstar Games said Friday (November 20, 2026), underscoring the enormous demand for the first new installment in the blockbuster series in 13 years.

headline: This 2D rhythm platformer video game is an ode to India’s multiplicities
body: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam in October.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”

This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

headline: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
body: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics
full_body:

Updated - November 21, 2026 12:05 am IST - Washington, D.C., United States

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).

The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.

It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.

As toddlers swiping through smartphone screens before holding a pencil has become a common sight, paediatricians are worried about an alarming trend: smartphones being increasingly used as “digital pacifiers” to appease toddlers during mealtime, soothe them when they throw a tantrum and keep them engaged while managing household chores. This phenomenon is no longer confined to urban households.

A study conducted by AIIMS Delhi, and published in the Indian Journal of Medical Research in April 2026, surveyed 282 children aged 2 to 4 years in rural Haryana. Its findings revealed that half of all the children surveyed exceeded the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) recommended screen time limit of an hour per day for children between 2 to 4 years. The research underlines a pervasive reliance on smartphones to keep children engaged, across all socio-economic layers.

headline: India’s smartphone sale plunged 22% during festive season
body: The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

As rising memory costs have been pushing smartphone prices to a new height, the impact of it was quite visible during the just concluded Indian festive season (October 8–November 10) which collapsed by an estimated 22% year-over-year (YoY), noted Counterpoint. The rising phone prices pushed a weaker demand as buyers held back their purchases.

“The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales,” the findings said.

The research firm highlighted that festive discounts narrowed to 10–25%, from 35–40% in 2025. “Even discounted entry-level models were generally priced higher than a year ago, putting upgrades out of reach for many price-sensitive buyers. Brands instead leaned on no-cost EMIs, bank offers and trade-ins, with 48% of smartphone sales being finance-led.”

During the first wave (October 8–18), volumes fell 19% YoY, with online sales falling short of the performance seen during earlier sale events. Online sales, which account for a significant share of smartphone purchases, declined as higher consumer traffic failed to translate into actual conversions.

During festive season also, Samsung had the best of lot with a 21% share, overtaking Vivo, as its sales fell 8% YoY against a 22% market decline. Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S25 drew strong demand, while Samsung delayed price hikes until after the sales and managed inventory better than rivals.

Vivo and Oppo declined 21% and 24%, respectively, holding up better in mainline retail through retailer incentives and bundled offers, but were weaker online.

headline: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮 💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
